stem:
Krish learns Gumulgal number names: urapon means 1 and ukasar means 2. Longer names are built as sums of these group words, so ukasar-urapon means 3 and ukasar-ukasar means 4.

Which reading of ukasar-ukasar-ukasar is correct?

options.text: The name means urapon, because urapon is the usual leftover word.
The name is just a new unrelated label, ignoring the known meanings of 1 and 2.
The name means 6, because it is $2 + 2 + 2$.
Treating the three parts as independent labels is what builds the total 6.

teacher.key_rationale: ukasar-ukasar-ukasar is three groups of 2, so 6. Calling it urapon swaps the group word. Ignoring 1 and 2 drops the naming rule. Saying independent labels build the total reverses how the sum is read.
